slides.title: The Counting House
slides.text: Welcome to the Counting House, where big numbers are built from small digits. The same digit can do very different jobs in different places.

visual.label: Big numbers are built from small digits: 3, 5, 2

focus.cue: Joined up, the digits build a big number: 352.

slides.title: Where a digit sits
slides.text: In 352, the 3 is not worth 3. It sits in the hundreds place, so it is worth 300. The 5 is worth 50, and the 2 is worth just 2.

visual.label: 352 in place value cards: 3 hundreds, 5 tens, 2 ones

focus.cue: The 3 sits in the hundreds place, so it is worth 300.
The 5 is worth 50, and the 2 is worth just 2.

slides.title: Rough first, then build
slides.text: Rough first: 2,463 is about 2,500, so our build should land near there. Now build it place by place.

visual.label: 2,463 built place by place: 2 thousands, 4 hundreds, 6 tens, 3 ones

slides.title: Stretch: Ten times the place
slides.text: In 55, the left 5 is worth ten times the right 5. Every step one place left makes a digit worth ten times more. Try it with 777.

visual.label: 55 in place value cards: 5 tens, 5 ones

focus.cue: The left 5 sits in the tens place: it is worth 50.
The right 5 sits in the ones place: it is worth 5.

words.means: one of the ten symbols 0 to 9 that build numbers
what a digit is worth because of where it sits
the place worth one hundred for each digit in it
a number written out as the sum of its place values

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Brain Board at Practice Board and score 3,000 points to finish. It opens straight on your place value board, and your board saves as you go. Get there your way: lots of easy tiles, or fewer hard ones. When a big number appears, read out its place values before you answer.
